name: Suriname
summary_text: Suriname demands real caution from trans visitors — legally unremarkable, socially mixed. Same-sex conduct is legal; the constitution's “any other status” clause is read to cover SOGI discrimination; and the 2022 Equal Treatment Labour Act added employment protections. There is no legal gender recognition and no documented trans-murder pattern, but Paramaribo's small community reports routine harassment, and the interior has essentially no protection. For a visitor: no legal exposure; modest street risk in Paramaribo; low tourist infrastructure generally.

sources.title: Suriname | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): Article 8.2 of the constitution prohibits discrimination including 'any other status' (argued to extend to SOGI); the 2022 Equal Treatment Labor Act explicitly bans SOGI discrimination at work; same-sex intercourse not criminalised; the penal code protects against hate speech; legal gender recognition advanced via the January 2022 appeals-court decision in De Staat Suriname v. Paris Yvanna Simson ordering registration changes for a trans woman.

Civil society report (Projekta Foundation with VIDS and LGBT Platform Suriname) to the UN Human Rights Committee's 141st session (July 2024) on ICCPR implementation in Suriname - includes non-discrimination and gender-equality sections covering LGBT issues.

US State Department 2015 Human Rights Report for Suriname: documents the Bouterse trial, police brutality, corruption, and 'discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and intersex (LGBTI) persons and other minorities'.

LGBT Platform Suriname + Akahatá + Heartland Alliance stakeholder report (Oct 2015) to the Human Rights Committee: the March 2015 Penal Code revisions (Articles 175, 175a, 176) added sexual-orientation protections (1 year jail or fine for discrimination), but implementation lags; government members' anti-gay positions and media/music-industry hostility perpetuate homophobia.

sources.title: Experts of the Human Rights Committee Commend Suriname for its Commitment to Judicial Independence, Ask about the National Human Rights Institute and the Rights of Tribal and Indig
sources.claim_summary: UN Geneva meeting summary (July 2024): Human Rights Committee experts commended Suriname's commitment to judicial independence during its fourth ICCPR periodic-report review, asking about the National Human Rights Institute and indigenous rights.

Suriname LGBT Platform UPR pre-session summary (March 2016): since the 2011 UPR, Suriname equalised the age of consent and added discrimination provisions (2015); but the pension act excludes same-sex couples from survivor pensions contrary to the constitution's non-discrimination principle; the Platform has never been included in consultative processes.
